claims.text: Permethrin 5% cream from the neck down, washed off after 8 to 14 hours;
claims.quote: Permethrin 5% cream applied to all areas of the body from the neck down and washed off after 8–14 hours
Older children and adults should apply permethrin to the entire body from the neck down and wash it off after 8 to 14 hours. Treatments should be repeated in 7 days.

claims.text: In infants and young children also the head and neck, avoiding the eyes and mouth
claims.quote: For infants and young children, permethrin should be applied to the head and neck, avoiding periorbital and perioral regions.

claims.text: Spinosad 0.9% suspension (age 4 and older) from the neck down, including the soles; leave on 6 hours; repeat in 1 week
claims.quote: For adults and children 4 years of age and older, spinosad 0.9% topical suspension should be applied to the entire cutaneous surface from the neck down, including the soles and feet (4). In patients who are bald, the suspension should be applied to the scalp, forehead, hairline, and temples. The suspension should be allowed to dry for 10 minutes before getting dressed and then left on the skin for 6 hours before showering or bathing. Treatment should be repeated in 1 week.

claims.text: Precipitated sulfur 6 to 10% in petrolatum: an alternative typically reserved for infants
claims.quote: Precipitated sulfur 6 to 10% in petrolatum is an alternative therapy typically reserved for infants

claims.text: Lindane: MSD says it is no longer recommended (neurotoxic);
claims.quote: Lindane is no longer recommended because it can be neurotoxic (5).

claims.text: CDC keeps it only for patients who can't tolerate, or have failed, recommended therapy.
claims.quote: Lindane is an alternative regimen because it can cause toxicity (1413); it should be used only if the patient cannot tolerate the recommended therapies or if these therapies have failed
